rationale: I picked the 40 highest-value targets by stacking four filters: demand=high, buying_intent=high, diy_friendly=true, and grounding strength (OEM/manufacturer or major-retailer parts sources). I deliberately spread across all nine categories to avoid clustering: washers (5), dryers (5), refrigerators (3), dishwashers (5), ranges/ovens (5), microwaves (3), furnaces (5), tankless water heaters (5), and mini-splits (4). I also balanced brands so no single OEM dominates - Samsung, LG, Whirlpool, GE, Frigidaire, Maytag, Bosch, KitchenAid appear across kitchen/laundry, while HVAC and water-heater brands (Carrier, Goodman, Trane, Rheem, York, Navien, Rinnai, Noritz, Mitsubishi, Daikin, MRCOOL) round out diversity. The top ranks prioritize the codes with the cleanest part-to-fix mapping and strongest commercial intent: drain pumps, water inlet valves, heating elements, evaporator fan motors, oven temperature sensors, and flame sensors/igniters - all parts a homeowner can buy and install, which maximizes affiliate/parts conversion. I dropped weaker-grounded or lower-intent entries (leak-sensor "LC/i30/E15" codes lean toward gaskets and condensation diagnosis with softer buying intent; thermostat codes like Nest N260/E74 and Honeywell E1 resolve to adapters/replacements rather than clear OEM parts; pure board-replacement codes like LG washer LE, Whirlpool F1E1, and inverter/compressor mini-split faults are not DIY-friendly). I held a handful of slugs for extra verification where the code identity or part mapping looked thinner.
